text:
Slovakia is once again preparing for a major cycling celebration. After successfully organizing the historic first-ever Youth European Championships and the European Cyclo-cross Cup, Slovakia has once again earned the trust of the European Cycling Union to host this prestigious event. In mid-November, the European Championships for Youth and Masters categories will take place at the x-bionic® sphere Olympic Sports Centre in Šamorín. For the second consecutive year, Slovakia will welcome the best cyclo-cross riders from across Europe — among them, perhaps, future Olympians of this sport, as cyclo-cross is set to become an Olympic discipline in 2030.

Less than a month remains until one of the biggest sporting events of the autumn season. After successfully organizing the historic first Youth European Championships and the European Cyclo-cross Cup in 2024, Slovak cycling has once again earned the trust and opportunity from the European Cycling Union to build on the success of these events. The upcoming European Championships for Youth and Masters categories are also the result of the active work of Peter Privara, President of the UEC Cyclo-cross Commission, and Katarína Jakubová, Vice President of the European Cycling Union. The event will take place at the x-bionic® sphere Olympic Sports Centre, which offers a comprehensive environment for hosting world-class sporting competitions.

Friday will be dedicated to the European Championships for Masters categories. After nine years, the European Championships for this age group return to Slovakia — the last edition took place in 2016 in Trnava. On Friday, medals will be contested in the following Masters categories: men 55–59, 60–64, 65–69, 70–74, and 75+, and women 35–39, 40–44, 45–49, 50–54, 55–59, 60–64, 65–69, and 70+.

Saturday will be dedicated to the European Championships for Youth categories — races for boys and girls aged 13 to 16, with each age group classified separately. In total, eight sets of medals will be awarded, similar to the Youth European Championships in mountain biking.

On Sunday, the cyclo-cross program will continue with final races of the youth categories — Men 15, Women 16, and Men 16 — followed by the Masters races. In the afternoon, the European titles will be decided among men Masters 50–54, 45–49, 40–44, and 35–39.

Peter Privara: "I am very pleased that we have once again gained the trust of the European Cycling Union and can organize the European Cyclo-cross Championships for youth and masters categories in Slovakia. Young people are the future of cyclo-cross, and we want to give them the opportunity to showcase their talent on the international stage.

Slovakia will once again present itself as a country that has a lot to offer – from high-quality organization to modern sports facilities. As president of the UEC Cyclo-cross Commission and the Slovak Cycling Federation, I am delighted that we are able to bring an event of this caliber to our country. Cyclo-cross has ambitions to become part of the Winter Olympics from 2030, and I believe that by organizing such championships, we are contributing to its growth and to the development of our competitors and organizers.

The last few years have been very successful for Slovak cyclo-cross, and I believe that thanks to the 2025 European Championships, the quality of our riders and organizers will improve even further. At the same time, I believe that this event will further strengthen Slovakia's place on the cycling map of Europe," concluded Peter Privara, President of the Slovak Cycling Federation and the UEC Cyclo-cross Commission.

Katarína Jakubová: "Cyclocross is one of the most dynamic and attractive cycling disciplines – I admit that it is also close to my heart. I am delighted that interest in this sport has been growing among young people in recent years. That is why we at the European Cycling Union have decided to create a separate European Youth Championship, which gives young riders the opportunity to gain their first major international experience and motivation to continue in cyclo-cross at the highest level.

Last year's success of the first ever edition in Šamorín confirmed that Slovakia not only has excellent organizational facilities, but also a heart for cyclo-cross. I am proud that we have once again gained the trust of the European Cycling Union and that the championship is returning to Slovakia – this time with the addition of the masters category. We plan to maintain this model within the UEC for the coming years.

I believe that another exceptional event awaits us, one that will leave its mark on the history of cyclo-cross and in the hearts of young competitors," said Katarína Jakubová, Vice-President of the European Cycling Union and Secretary General of the Slovak Cycling Federation.
